7.3.16      NRST pin characteristics
            The NRST pin input driver uses CMOS technology. It is connected to a permanent pull-up
            resistor, RPU (see Table 147: I/O static characteristics).
            Unless otherwise specified, the parameters given in Table 152 are derived from tests
            performed under the ambient temperature and VDD supply voltage conditions summarized
            in Table 112: General operating conditions.

                                                 Table 152. NRST pin characteristics
                 Symbol                    Parameter                     Conditions             Min       Typ    Max     Unit

                              Weak pull-up equivalent
                  RPU(2)                                                   VIN = VSS             30        40    50       kΩ
                              resistor(1)
                VF(NRST)(2) NRST Input filtered pulse                1.71 V < VDD < 3.6 V         -         -    50
                                                                     1.71 V < VDD < 3.6 V        300        -     -       ns
             VNF(NRST)(2) NRST Input not filtered pulse
                                                                     1.62 V < VDD < 3.6 V       1000        -     -
            1. The pull-up is designed with a true resistance in series with a switchable PMOS. This PMOS contribution
               to the series resistance must be minimum (~10% order).
            2. Guaranteed by design.

            1. The reset network protects the device against parasitic resets.
            2. The user must ensure that the level on the NRST pin can go below the VIL(NRST) max level specified in
               Table 147. Otherwise the reset is not taken into account by the device.


7.3.17      FMC characteristics
            Unless otherwise specified, the parameters given in Table 153 to Table 166 for the FMC
            interface are derived from tests performed under the ambient temperature, fHCLK frequency
            and VDD supply voltage conditions summarized in Table 112: General operating conditions,
            with the following configuration:
            •      Output speed is set to OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 11
            •      Measurement points are done at CMOS levels: 0.5VDD
            •      IO Compensation cell activated.
            •      HSLV activated when VDD ≤ 2.7 V
            •      VOS level set to VOS1.
